sources.label: If the Contractor installs defective materials, equipment, or performs work that deviates from specifications or drawings, the Architect issues a written directive requiring removal and replacement
The Contractor must comply without additional compensation unless a Change Order is issued
If removal requires demolition of adjacent completed work, the Contractor must perform the demolition and restoration at the Contractor's cost, as the defect is the Contractor's responsibility
The Architect may require the Contractor to remove and replace work even if the Owner is not present or has not seen the defect
The Owner is not required to inspect or approve each component before it is covered; the Architect's directive, based on the contract requirements, is sufficient
However, if the Architect allows defective work to be covered (e.g., concrete poured over defective rebar placement, walls painted over unfinished surface preparation)
sources.description: the Architect may later be unable to require removal without demolishing adjacent components, reducing the practicality of correction
